title: AI Business Analysis and Process Discovery

questions.question: What is the risk of AI-generated business analysis summaries?
options: They always ask too many clarifying questions before producing any summary at all — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
They can create false confidence when stakeholders, variants, or evidence are missing
They cannot mention process variants even when multiple variants clearly exist
They automatically remove every assumption the analyst had made along the way
questions.explanation: A clean AI summary can create false confidence when stakeholders, variants, or evidence are actually missing — it's not about asking too many questions, being unable to mention variants, or removing assumptions.

questions.question: Interview notes describe how the approval process works in one region, but the analysis never checks whether other regions handle the same approval differently. Which of the lesson's four signals does this match most directly?
options: Stakeholder gap — someone who could describe the process accurately was never interviewed
Process variant — the same process may work differently across teams or regions, unchecked
Requirement ambiguity — it's unclear what the approval process is actually supposed to require
Evidence missing — no source document backs up the described process steps
questions.explanation: Never checking whether other regions handle the same process differently is the lesson's process-variant signal — distinct from a stakeholder gap, requirement ambiguity, or missing evidence.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A final, signed contract ready to be sent to the client for approval
A fully deployed workflow running in the production process engine
A test runner that automatically validates the discovered requirements
A ranked business-analysis discovery plan with controls for each gap
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks discovery gaps into a business-analysis plan with controls such as interview guide or evidence register — it doesn't produce a contract, a deployed workflow, or a test runner.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: Hiding evidence gaps so the analysis reads as more complete than it is
Skipping stakeholder interviews because the process documentation already exists
Assumption log — separates confirmed facts from claims that still need checking
Removing process variants from the analysis to keep the write-up simple
questions.explanation: The lesson's controls are interview guide, process variant map, assumption log, and evidence register — an assumption log separates confirmed facts from unresolved claims, unlike hiding evidence, skipping stakeholders, or dropping variants.

questions.question: When should AI-assisted analysis move into a discovery workshop?
options: When impact and ambiguity are high and multiple discovery gaps still exist
Only when every requirement is already completely clear and confirmed — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Only when there is no stakeholder available to interview at all
Never — a clean AI summary can substitute for a discovery workshop
questions.explanation: High impact and ambiguity with multiple open discovery gaps is when analysis should move into a workshop — not when everything is already clear, no stakeholder exists, or a summary is treated as a substitute.

questions.question: What should an evidence register capture?
options: Only the final solution ideas that emerged from the discovery process
Only the raw AI-generated text summarizing the interview notes
Sources, examples, confirmations, and any open evidence gaps
No source references, since citations only slow down the analysis
questions.explanation: An evidence register should capture sources, examples, confirmations, and open evidence gaps — not just solution ideas, raw AI text, or a register with no source references.
